lines.text: What happens if you hook a dead car battery up to a welder?
This battery should make 825 amps but it only makes 204 which isn't even lawnmower power.
beats: ai:a small red push lawn mower on green grass at golden hour

lines.text: Because when a battery sits dead crystals grow on its lead plates and the acid can't reach the metal.
beats: ai:extreme macro of grey lead plates inside a car battery covered in white fuzzy crystals
ai:macro of white sulfate crystals slowly growing over dark metal
ai:macro of clear acid droplets stopped by a wall of white crystals on a lead plate

lines.text: So he hits it with 85 amps which is almost ten times a normal charger to shake them loose.
beats: ai:a small household car battery charger on a garage shelf

lines.text: And those bubbles are hydrogen and oxygen so it's basically a bomb in a box.
beats: ai:a black car battery shaped like a cartoon bomb with a lit sparkling fuse

lines.text: But six rounds later it's only up to 446 and it still can't start the tractor.
So he tries the internet's favorite fix with Epsom salt but to add it he drains the acid.
Which is like filling your gas tank with bath water so it drops from 600 amps to 51.
beats: ai:an open car gas tank filled to the top with soapy bath water and foam
ai:a bathtub full of foamy bath water

lines.text: But battery five starts at just 62 amps and after six rounds on the welder it hits 961 which is fifteen times stronger.
And it cranks a big block V8 for thirteen straight seconds.
beats: ai:a huge chrome big block V8 engine in a dark garage

lines.text: The catch is it fixes crystals and not damage because another battery died again overnight.
beats: ai:blue electric sparks shattering white crystals on a lead plate macro
ai:macro of a cracked broken lead plate inside a car battery

lines.text: So would you hook your dead battery up to a welder?
